raw:
I haven't run these against the benchmark data, so they come from my prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201. Most are replace-`none` effects: setting an edge to a conv op gains more when it replaces `none` than when it replaces another op. The last two are path-redundancy effects: a conv edit matters more when the alternative parallel path is weak.
